title: Pre-Trip Inspection Checklist for Saskatoon Delivery & Landscaping Fleets
body:
Whether you are running a landscaping crew across Sutherland or managing a delivery route through downtown Saskatoon, a thorough pre-trip inspection keeps your fleet running smoothly and your drivers safe. This checklist covers the essentials every delivery and landscaping business should follow before vehicles hit the road.

**Why Pre-Trip Inspections Matter for Local Fleets**

Saskatoon experiences harsh winters with heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures, followed by hot summers with dust and gravel roads. These conditions put extra stress on fleet vehicles, making consistent pre-trip inspections critical for local businesses. A quick check before each shift can catch small problems before they become costly breakdowns, keep your drivers safe, and ensure timely deliveries for your customers.

**Exterior Walk-Around**

Start by walking completely around each vehicle. Check that all headlights, taillights, brake lights, and turn signals are functioning properly. Saskatoon streets can be dark during winter commutes, so proper lighting is essential for safety. Inspect tires for adequate tread depth and proper inflation—cold Saskatchewan mornings cause tire pressure to drop, so check PSI when tires are cold. Look for any visible damage such as cracks in windshields, missing mirrors, or dented body panels that could affect visibility or safety.

**Under the Hood**

Open the hood and check fluid levels. Engine oil should be between the minimum and maximum marks on the dipstick. Coolant levels should be visible in the overflow tank, and windshield washer fluid should be topped up, especially before winter driving when road salt and slush reduce visibility. Inspect belts and hoses for signs of cracking, fraying, or leaks. In landscaping trucks carrying equipment, ensure that all toolSecurement straps and trailer hitches are in good condition and properly connected.

**Brakes and Steering**

Test the brake pedal for proper firmness and listen for any unusual sounds when applying brakes. A soft pedal or squealing can indicate worn brake pads or air in the brake lines. Check steering for excessive play or unusual resistance. Saskatoon drivers encounter icy intersections and uneven pavement, making reliable brakes and responsive steering essential for safe fleet operations.

**Interior Checks**

Inside the cab, verify that all warning lights on the dashboard illuminate briefly when the ignition is turned on and then go off. Check that the horn, wipers, and rearview mirrors are functioning. Ensure seat belts are operational and free of damage. For delivery vehicles making frequent stops, confirm that backup cameras and sensors are working properly to prevent accidents in busy Saskatoon parking lots.

**Emergency and Safety Equipment**

Verify that the first aid kit is stocked and accessible. Check that a functioning fire extinguisher is mounted securely. Ensure reflective triangles or flares are present in case of a breakdown on rural routes near Saskatoon. These items are not just good practice—they are often required for commercial vehicles.

**Documentation and Logs**

Record your inspection findings on a fleet inspection form. Note any issues discovered and report them immediately to your maintenance team. Keeping written logs demonstrates due diligence and helps identify recurring problems with specific vehicles in your fleet.

**Making Inspections a Daily Habit**

Post this checklist in your shop or break room so drivers can reference it easily. Consider designating a specific time before each shift for inspections, treating it as a non-negotiable part of the workday rather than an afterthought. This habit reduces unexpected repairs, protects your drivers, and keeps your Saskatoon fleet reliable day after day.

Regular pre-trip inspections are one of the simplest ways to maintain your fleet, reduce downtime, and serve your customers safely across Saskatoon and surrounding communities.
